2	
3	Own the Frontend layer of the synthetic ticket board.
4	
5	> **Human reading this:** run `/grill-my-role` in your AI editor, or paste
6	> to your agent: _"Read .grill-with-me/MY-ROLE.md and follow it."_ Then just answer the
7	> questions — about ten minutes. Everything below is addressed to the agent.
8	
9	## What you own
10	- src/TicketList.ts
11	
12	## Before we start
13	Read `grill/PROJECT.md`, any `grill/*-spec.md` files your teammates have
14	already committed, and the repo you are standing in.
15	
16	## The grill
17	
18	Interview me relentlessly about MY LAYER ONLY — the "Frontend" role —
19	until we reach a shared understanding of what I am building and what I need
20	from the other roles. Walk down each branch of the decision tree, resolving
21	dependencies between decisions one by one. For each question, provide your
22	recommended answer. Ask one question at a time — multiple questions at once
23	is bewildering.
24	
25	If a fact can be found in the repo, look it up rather than asking me. The
26	decisions are mine.
27	
28	Prefer questions that reference something real: code that already exists in
29	this repo, or something a teammate wrote in their spec. If my answer
30	contradicts a teammate's committed spec, point at the exact line and ask
31	which of us should change.
32	Only call it a contradiction when the two statements are incompatible.
33	A teammate omitting a detail (such as a column default) does not reject it.
34	
35	Make sure we cover:
36	- Close failure presentation
37	- Refresh behavior
38	
39	Keep a short running summary of what you have understood so far, and show it
40	to me every few questions so I can correct drift early.
41	
42	Keep observed repo behavior, teammate commitments, my explicit answers, and
43	your recommendations distinct. A recommendation becomes my decision only when
44	I explicitly accept it. Saying "I'm done" ends the interview; it does not
45	accept an unanswered recommendation or authorize you to choose its details.
46	
47	## When I say I'm done
48	
49	Write `grill/frontend-spec.md` containing EXACTLY these five headings once
50	each, in this order, outside code fences. Individual sections may be empty;
51	a spec empty under every heading is invalid:
52	
53	## Scope
54	## What I own
55	## What I need from other roles
56	## Decisions made
57	## Still unclear
58	
59	Under each heading, be concrete: name endpoints as METHOD /path with request
60	and response shapes, name tables and columns with types, name files by path.
61	"An endpoint that returns items" is useless; `POST /api/rank` returning
62	`{ trails: { id: string; shadeScore: number }[] }` is what the contract
63	needs. Do not invent agreements I did not make — anything not yet agreed
64	belongs under "Still unclear".
65	
66	Describe existing code as observed behavior, not as a decision to preserve or
67	replace it. Record only explicitly chosen changes under "Decisions made".
68	Do not choose new function return shapes, status handling, retry behavior,
69	rendering, or refresh mechanisms just to make the spec concrete. If my answer
70	does not specify one, keep that detail under "Still unclear". For example,
71	"reload" alone does not agree a full page reload or a particular fetch/result
72	shape. State dependencies under "What I need from other roles" as requests
73	until the relevant role has agreed; also list their pending agreement under
74	"Still unclear". Do not claim a teammate approved or implemented a request.
75	
76	Run `npx grill-with-me check-spec grill/frontend-spec.md` after writing it.
77	If validation fails, correct the structure or report the missing decisions
78	before telling me to commit. Surface thin-section warnings; never invent
79	agreements just to make a section longer.

2	name: check-contract
3	description: Check the repo against grill/CONTRACT.md and report drift attributed to a role. Anyone on the team can run this, repeatedly, during the build.
4	---
5	
6	You are checking whether the code matches what the team agreed. Your report
7	tells the person who runs you **who to go talk to** — findings are grouped
8	by role, never presented as a bare file list.
9	
10	## Step 0 — revision integrity, freshness, and pending agreement
11	
12	- Run `npx grill-with-me contract-status` before checking code. Record its exact
13	  revision ID and freshness: fresh means local source/artifact hashes match;
14	  stale means source hashes changed; unknown means source comparison is
15	  unavailable or integrity/recovery is incomplete. Never compare a room's
16	  packVersion with a contract revision. Offline unknown is unverified freshness,
17	  not confirmed drift. Stop on integrity conflicts or unfinished finalization;
18	  do not produce a clean report against mixed prose/types/history.
19	- Read `.grill-with-me/member.json` if present.
20	- This local receipt also names the role this checkout joined as. Put that role's
21	  findings first in the report: they are the only ones the person running
22	  you can fix without going to find someone.
23	- If local state is absent, do not infer a current role from legacy shared
24	  `grill/.room`, `grill/MY-ROLE.md`, or a teammate's spec. Report all roles evenly.
25	- Read `grill/CONTRACT-HISTORY.jsonl` and `grill/CONTRACT-CHANGES.md`.
26	  The current CONTRACT.md is the current truth;
27	  finalized amendments are already applied there. Pending roles in status must
28	  remain visibly pending even when file hashes are fresh. History is an audit
29	  trail, not a second competing version to silently overlay. For legacy
30	  unrecorded contracts, flag freshness unknown and request explicit adoption;
31	  surface prose/history contradictions for reconciliation rather than guessing.
32	
33	## Step 1 — scope the check
34	
35	Do NOT read the whole repo. Derive the file set from the contract itself:
36	
37	1. Every implementing file named in `## Endpoints`
38	2. Files defining the tables/models named in `## Data model`
39	3. Call sites of contract endpoints — grep for each endpoint path literal
40	   and each `Paths` constant usage
41	4. If `grill/contract.ts` exists, run
42	   `npx grill-with-me contract-typecheck <consuming-tsconfig>` first. This uses
43	   the project's installed compiler and real declared typecheck command, plus
44	   selected-project diagnostics. Choose each leaf config in a solution repo.
45	   No compiler/config means unknown; missing or unused imports mean
46	   unintegrated. Neither is a clean typed check. Never automatically download
47	   TypeScript or compile only the generated file. Use the reported consumers
48	   and concrete diagnostics to scope findings; compare existing baseline errors.
49	   Bound imports do not prove both sides of every endpoint use the contract or
50	   establish runtime behavior. Inspect producer/caller boundaries explicitly.
51	
52	If a contract file does not exist yet in the repo, that is a finding
53	("endpoint agreed but not implemented"), not a reason to search elsewhere.
54	
55	## Step 2 — compare
56	
57	For each contract line, check the implementation:
58	
59	- Field names and shapes in responses vs the contract's response shape
60	- Request parsing vs the contract's request shape
61	- Table/column names vs the data model
62	- Who writes state that another role owns
63	- Error behavior where the contract specifies it
64	
65	Only report what you can evidence with a file and line. If you cannot read
66	enough to be sure, say "unverified", never guess. A clean repo must produce
67	an empty report — do not manufacture findings to seem useful.
68	
69	## Step 3 — write grill/CHECK-REPORT.md
70	
71	```markdown
72	# Contract check — <date>
73	_Against contract revision <ID or unrecorded>; freshness <fresh/stale/unknown>; typed integration <result>. M files in scope._
74	
75	## Pending agreement
76	- <revision ID and roles still pending, or none>
77	
78	## ⚠️ <Role name>
79	- `path/to/file.ts:LINE` — what the code does vs what the contract says.
80	  → Talk to <other role> before changing either side.
81	  Outcome: [ ] fix the code   [ ] contract is wrong → run amend-contract   [ ] accepted, ignore
82	
83	## ✅ <Role name>
84	- No drift detected.
85	
86	## Unverified
87	- <anything you could not check, and why>
88	```
89	
90	Every finding offers the three outcomes above — drift is sometimes the
91	contract's fault, and the fix for that is `amend-contract`, not a code
92	change. If a previous CHECK-REPORT.md exists, carry forward its "accepted"
93	markings and label findings not present last time as **NEW**.
94	
95	Finish by summarizing: how many findings, how many new, and — if any —
96	which single conversation between two people would clear the most items.
97

I've read the role brief, the project context, the backend spec, and the code I own. One tooling note first:

- `node .eval-cli/grill.mjs contract-status` fails here — `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, the `.eval-cli/grill.mjs` file doesn't exist in this checkout. I'm reporting that rather than hunting for another path. It doesn't block the grill: there's no `grill/CONTRACT.md` yet, so we're still in the grilling phase, and contract freshness is **unknown** (unverified, not confirmed drift).

**What I observed in the repo (facts, not decisions):**
- `src/TicketList.ts:1-5` — `loadTickets(fetcher)` calls `fetcher("/api/tickets")`, does `response.json()`, returns `body.tickets`. No status check, no error branch.
- `src/TicketList.ts:6-8` — `closeTicket(fetcher, id)` POSTs to `"/api/tickets/" + id + "/close"` and returns the raw `Response`. It never reads the body, never inspects `response.status`.
- `src/api.ts` is a hardcoded stub (`listTickets` returns one `t1` "Demo" ticket); `src/auth.ts:1` returns the literal string `'not yet agreed'`.
- `db/schema.sql:1` has `closed BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`.

**What Backend has committed** (`grill/backend-spec.md`): `GET /api/tickets` → `{ tickets: { id, title, closed }[] }`; `POST /api/tickets/:id/close` → `{ id: string; closed: boolean }`; missing ticket → HTTP 404 `{ error: "not_found" }`; authentication explicitly *not* agreed.

So the paths and the list shape my code already uses line up with Backend's spec. The open ground is what happens when a close *fails*, and what the list does afterward.

---

**Question 1 of the grill — close failure presentation.**

Backend committed a concrete failure case I can actually hit: `POST /api/tickets/:id/close` → HTTP 404 with `{ error: "not_found" }` (`grill/backend-spec.md:9`). But `closeTicket` at `src/TicketList.ts:7` hands the caller the raw `Response` and never looks at `status`, so today a 404 is indistinguishable from a success at the call site.

When a close fails, what should the member see?

My recommendation: show an inline error next to the ticket row that failed — not a global banner, not a silent no-op — and leave that ticket visibly open. Rationale: the demo must show "close a ticket" (`grill/PROJECT.md:10`), so a failure that looks like a success is the worst outcome, and row-local placement tells the member *which* ticket didn't close when several are on screen.

Two things I will *not* decide for you, and will park under "Still unclear" unless you say otherwise: the wording of the message, and whether `closeTicket` changes its return shape to carry that failure (right now it returns `Response`; changing that is a real decision, not a formatting detail).
